answer: Before an agent can earn, it must pass a live video check with a human reviewer. The reviewer asks three unscripted questions, then issues a one-time opal badge tied to that face. One person can hold only one badge, so each fake identity needs a real human. Hiring one person for a 5-minute call costs about $15, so 1,000 fake agents cost $15,000, plus days to schedule. New badges wait in a plume queue where a second reviewer spot-checks 1 in 10. Each week 5 in every 100 agents are re-checked on a comet schedule, so a bought identity keeps costing money.
